failure_modes: Diffusion of responsibility among agents who each expect another path to deliver
Removing redundant noisy pathways in the name of efficiency and creating a single point of failure
Mistaking illusion of control through one owner for actual reliability
gloss: Make an outcome reliable through many noisy ways to reach it, not one accountable path
invariants: The probability of an outcome rises with the number of distinct paths that reach it
Individual pathways may be unreliable while the aggregate is reliable
mechanism: An outcome with many routes to it is more likely than one with a single route, as seven is likelier than double six with two dice, and as balls on a Galton board pile up in the middle. Biological systems get reliable results from many unreliable pathways, such as an apoptosis signal that fires in about 92% of cells. Human organisations prefer one assigned owner with incentives and accountability, which creates a single point of failure. Reliability can instead come from the law of large numbers acting on many partial, overlapping ways of getting the work done.
